The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.238/2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Irinjalakuda, is the appellant herein in MACA No.2031/2017 and the 3rd respondent therein is the Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Sribil on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188893106/

sentences.text:
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 14.10.2010.

According to the petitioner, on 14.10.2010 at about 8.15 a.m., while he was riding a motorcycle bearing reg.no.KL AG 2885, a car bearing reg.no.KL 45 A 8790 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.1,25,05,000/- limited to Rs.1,00,00,000/-.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A23 and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.40,59,536/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner & 3rd respondent preferred these appeals.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.P.V.Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. Mathews Jacob, the learned Senior Counsel as instructed by Sri.P.Jacob Mathew, the Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

In the accident the 2025:KER:30412 MACA NO.2031 OF 2017 & MACA NO. 1445 OF 2017 petitioner sustained the following injuries:

9. Ext.A4 is his scan report.
As per the scan report the following findings were reached.

Comminuted fracture anterior, medial and postero lateral walls of both maxillary sinuses Extending to involve both ptergoid plates  Fracture both nasal bones and the nasal septum  Fracture body of mandible adjacent to the symphysis  Subcondylar fracture of the left mandibular condyle with left tempero mandibular joint dislocation.
 Minimal sub arachnoid hemorrhage  Minimal pneumocephalus
Minimal left pleural effusion
No ascitis at present
Normal sonographis appearance of liver, gallbladder, spleen and left kidney.

The fracture line is extending inferiority along the quadrilateral plate to the ischeal tuberosity.
Posterior fracture dislocation of right hip joint with marked displacement of the femoral head.
Multiple small intra articular fragments within the fight hip joint.

11. As per Exhibit X1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the petitioner suffered 45%
psychological disability and 17% orthopedic disability and the whole body disability was assessed as 53.5%.

However, considering the condition and gravity of the injuries sustained by the petitioner,
the Tribunal, has fixed his functional disability at 100%.
Aggrieved by the above assessment of functional disability at 100%, the 3 rd respondent preferred this appeal.

12. According to the learned Senior counsel appearing for the 3 rd respondent the Tribunal was not justified in fixing the functional disability of the petitioner at 100% as the medical board assessed only 53.5% disability.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that 2025:KER:30412 MACA NO.2031 OF 2017 & MACA NO. 1445 OF 2017 because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner who was working as meter reader in the KSEB, lost his employment and as such the Tribunal was justified in fixing the functional disability at 100%.
13. Further according to him, the Tribunal has not awarded future prospects to the monthly income and as such the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
14. Exts.A14 is the certificate issued from the KSEB stating that the petitioner was on unauthorised absence from duty from 13.12.2011 onwards.

Ext .A19 is the order of the Chief Engineer, Human Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Sribil on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188893106/
4 Resource Management, KSEB, terminating the service of the petitioner w.e.f. 06.10.2012, the date of unauthorised absence.

sentences.text: The Tribunal specifically found that the petition failed to attend duty because of the psychological disability suffered by him on account of the injuries sustained in the accident.
I do not find any grounds to interfere with the above
The learned counsel for the petitioner has passed over to this Court some medical bills showing that even now the petitioner is under psychiatric treatment in Amrutha Institute of Medical Science.

Therefore, considering the fact that, in the accident the petitioner sustained very serious injury including 9 fractures and because of the injuries he suffered psychological disability and because of the 2025:KER:30412 MACA NO.2031 OF 2017 &
MACA NO. 1445 OF 2017 psychological disability he even lost his employment as meter reader in KSEB, the Tribunal was justified in fixing his functional disability at 100%.
15. The monthly salary of the petitioner was Rs.15771/- and the same is not in dispute.
Ext.A22 is the letter dated 20/01/2017 issued by the KSEB, it is revealed that if the petitioner was in service he would have received Rs.36,428/- in December 2016.
In spite of the production of Ext.A22, the Tribunal has not added any income towards his future prospects.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to get 50% addition towards future prospects.
16. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 24 years.

Therefore, 50% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.51,09,804/-.
17.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/-, but nothing was awarded towards 'loss of amenities of life'.

In the accident the petitioner sustained very serious injuries including 9 fractures, he was treated as inpatient for 66 days and in the meantime he had 2025:KER:30412 MACA NO.2031 OF 2017 & MACA NO. 1445 OF 2017 undergone a surgery also.
Further, he had suffered 100% functional disability and he even lost his employment.
Therefore, the compensation awarded on the head 'pain and suffering' is on the lower side.

For the same reasons,
the Tribunal was also not justified in not awarding compensation on the head 'loss of amenities of life'.
Considering the facts, towards pain and suffering Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded and towards 'loss of amenities' Rs.3,00,000/- is awarded.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.61,62,804/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

In the result, MACA 2031 is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.61,62,804/- (Rupees Sixty One Lakhs Sixty Two Thousand Eight Hundred and Four only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @ 8%)
21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse 25% of the entire amount, excluding court fee payable, if any, to the petitioner, forthwith.

22. The Tribunal is permitted to decide, after considering the welfare, well being and the best interest of the petitioner, whether the balance amount is to be disbursed in full, forthwith or in installments or to be deposited in a Nationalised bank in fixed deposit in the name of the petitioner and to permit withdrawal of interest alone for the time being.
In the result.
MACA 1445 of 2017 is dismissed, without costs.
